mcqs.q: Aging is best described as:
opts: A progressive generalized impairment of function with loss of adaptive response to stress
A disease that can be cured
mcqs.explain: Aging is a normal, inevitable biological process — a progressive generalized impairment of function with loss of adaptive response to stress and growing risk of age-associated disease.

mcqs.q: The FASTEST-growing population segment in most countries is:
opts: Adults older than 80 years (≈20% of the world by 2050)
mcqs.explain: The fastest-growing segment is adults older than 80, which the UN estimates will make up nearly 20% of the world's population.

mcqs.q: In Saudi Arabia by 2050, people aged 60+ are predicted to be:
mcqs.explain: The proportion of people in Saudi Arabia aged 60+ is predicted to be 25% of the total ~40 million population by 2050.

mcqs.q: The overall trend in oral health of older adults is that:
opts: It is improving — periodontal disease and caries rates have decreased
mcqs.explain: Oral health is improving; rates of periodontal disease and caries have decreased for most age groups.

mcqs.q: A major factor improving older adults' oral health is:
opts: Fluoridation (water, toothpaste, rinses, gels) and better access
mcqs.explain: Contributing factors include fluoridation through community water, toothpaste, rinses and gels, treatment advances, improved hygiene and access.

mcqs.q: ‘Edentulism’ is an important oral-health indicator because it affects:
opts: Quality of life, self-esteem and nutritional status
mcqs.explain: Edentulism (complete tooth loss) is one of the most important indicators of oral health — it affects quality of life, self-esteem and nutritional status.

mcqs.q: Which behavioral risk factor is linked to ~30% of all cancers?
mcqs.explain: Smoking is related to periodontal disease and poor oral health and contributes to the development of 30% of all cancers.

mcqs.q: Elevated salivary cortisol (linking stress to oral disease) is associated with:
opts: Periodontal disease and temporomandibular joint dysfunction
mcqs.explain: Stress raises salivary cortisol, linked to the extent/severity of periodontal disease and TMJ dysfunction.

mcqs.q: One FUNCTIONAL effect of aging on dental care is that:
opts: Dental insurance often ceases upon retirement
Patients gain free care for life
mcqs.explain: Functional status declines with increased disability, reducing the ability to maintain hygiene and access care; dental insurance often ceases upon retirement.

mcqs.q: Many medications taken by older adults (antihypertensives, anticoagulants, antidepressants) commonly cause:
mcqs.explain: Saliva is crucial for oral health; medications such as antihypertensives, anticoagulants and antidepressants commonly cause xerostomia (dry mouth).

mcqs.q: Alzheimer's disease and other dementias affect oral health because patients:
opts: Do not view dental care as a priority and have declining oral hygiene
mcqs.explain: Patients with dementia may not view dental care as a high priority, have limited self-awareness of needs, and show a decline in oral hygiene practices.

mcqs.q: Which physiological change of aging affects treatment outcomes?
opts: Decreased healing, immunity and saliva, plus polypharmacy
mcqs.explain: Physiological changes — decreased healing, immunity and saliva, plus polypharmacy — all affect treatment outcomes.

mcqs.q: ‘Polypharmacy’ means:
mcqs.explain: Polypharmacy = the use of multiple drugs, common in older adults and affecting oral health/treatment.

mcqs.q: The MAJOR cause of tooth loss in older adults is:
mcqs.explain: Root caries is a major cause of tooth loss in older adults.

mcqs.q: The root surface is MORE susceptible to caries than enamel because cementum and dentin are:
mcqs.explain: Root surface cementum and dentin are more susceptible to cavitation because they are less mineralized than enamel.

mcqs.q: Dental caries is caused by bacteria that:
opts: Feed on carbohydrates and produce acids that dissolve tooth mineral
mcqs.explain: Caries bacteria (e.g. S. mutans, S. sobrinus, lactobacilli) feed on carbohydrates and produce acids that dissolve the mineral content of the tooth.

mcqs.q: Which restorative material releases fluoride and suits atraumatic restorative treatment of root caries?
mcqs.explain: Glass ionomer / RMGI contain and release fluoride into saliva and adjacent tooth structure (atraumatic restorative treatment).

mcqs.q: An advantage of AMALGAM for restoring root caries is:
mcqs.explain: Amalgam offers greater longevity and lower costs; resin bonding (composite) needs isolation and saliva control, which is difficult near the gingival margin.

mcqs.q: Periodontal disease is an inflammatory disease caused by:
opts: Gram-negative anaerobic bacteria from dental plaque
mcqs.explain: Periodontal disease is an inflammatory disease caused by gram-negative anaerobic bacteria from dental plaque.

mcqs.q: Periodontal disease progresses to PERIODONTITIS when inflammation extends to the:
mcqs.explain: It becomes periodontitis when inflammation extends to the periodontal ligament and alveolar bone → recession, bone loss, tooth mobility/loss.

mcqs.q: ‘Xerostomia’ is:
opts: A subjective sensation of oral dryness
mcqs.explain: Xerostomia (xero = dry, stomia = mouth) is a subjective sensation of oral dryness, often associated with salivary gland hypofunction.

mcqs.q: Which statement about xerostomia is TRUE?
opts: It is very common in older adults but NOT a normal part of aging
It is a normal, expected feature of aging
mcqs.explain: Xerostomia is a very common complaint among older adults, but it is not a normal part of the aging process.

mcqs.q: For oral cancer in older adults, the priority is:
opts: Early diagnosis with close attention and monitoring
mcqs.explain: Oral cancer can develop in the mouth; early diagnosis is crucial, so an at-risk older adult requires close attention and monitoring.

mcqs.q: Successful complete-denture treatment ULTIMATELY depends on the patient's:
opts: Ability and willingness to accept and learn to use dentures
mcqs.explain: The patient's ability and willingness to accept and learn to use dentures ultimately determine the success of clinical treatment.

mcqs.q: When planning treatment for an older adult with hearing/cognitive decline, you should:
opts: Speak slowly, use visual aids, and involve the caregiver/family
mcqs.explain: Geriatric patients may have hearing impairment and cognitive decline — speak slowly, use visual aids, and involve a caregiver/family member.

mcqs.q: A guiding principle of treatment planning for the older adult is:
mcqs.explain: Treatment planning principles: modify, don't deny; short appointments; morning visits; stress reduction; patient comfort is key.

mcqs.q: Which appointment approach best suits the older adult?
opts: Short, morning appointments with stress reduction
mcqs.explain: Short appointments, morning visits and stress reduction (with patient comfort as key) are recommended.

mcqs.q: Preventive strategies emphasised for older adults include:
opts: Fluoride therapy, oral hygiene, diet counseling and recall visits
mcqs.explain: Preventive strategies: fluoride therapy, oral hygiene, diet counseling and recall visits.

mcqs.q: Which ETHICAL consideration is important when treating older adults?
mcqs.explain: Ethical considerations include informed consent and elder-abuse awareness.

mcqs.q: Learning to accept and use a complete denture is a complex process requiring:
opts: Adaptation of learning, muscular skill and motivation
mcqs.explain: Accepting and using a complete denture is complex — it requires adaptation of learning, muscular skill and motivation; the patient's ability and willingness determine success.

saqs.q: Define aging and describe the demographic trend.
saqs.a: Aging = a natural, inevitable, progressive generalized impairment of function, with loss of adaptive response to stress and growing risk of age-associated disease. Demographically the population is aging fast — the over-80s are the fastest-growing segment (≈20% of the world by 2050); in Saudi Arabia the 60+ may reach ~25% by 2050.

saqs.q: List the behavioral oral-systemic risk factors in geriatric patients.
saqs.a: Diet (high fat/carb, low fibre), Smoking, Stress (raised salivary cortisol), Alcohol, poor Hygiene, and Physical inactivity.

saqs.q: List the physiological changes of aging that affect dental treatment.
saqs.a: Decreased healing, decreased immunity, decreased saliva, and polypharmacy (multiple drugs) — these affect treatment outcomes.

saqs.q: List the common oral conditions in older adults and briefly describe root caries.
saqs.a: Common conditions: root caries, periodontal (gum) disease, xerostomia, oral cancer, edentulism. Root caries is a major cause of tooth loss; bacteria produce acids that dissolve mineral, and the root surface (cementum/dentin) is more susceptible because it is less mineralized than enamel.

saqs.q: What is xerostomia, and is it a normal part of aging?
saqs.a: Xerostomia (xero = dry, stomia = mouth) is a subjective sensation of oral dryness, often associated with salivary gland hypofunction and altered saliva. It is very common in older adults but is NOT a normal part of the aging process.

saqs.q: Give the treatment-planning principles for the older adult.
saqs.a: Modify, don't deny; short appointments; morning visits; stress reduction; patient comfort is key. Communicate well (speak slowly, visual aids, involve caregiver), mind ethics (consent, elder-abuse), and focus on prevention (fluoride, hygiene, diet, recall).
